_about: Named color grades as ffmpeg filter chains, applied by pipeline/footage.py when footage is staged (baked into the clip, so preview and render always agree and no GPU is needed). Names follow styles/LEXICON.md. Each chain runs in RGB on 8-bit video; 'grain' (0..1) and 'vignette' (0..1) are finishing defaults the --grain/--vignette flags override. Compare them on your own frame: python3 pipeline/footage.py --project <dir> --grade-sheet <clip>

neutral.notes: A gentle S-curve and a touch of saturation. Fixes flat phone footage without announcing a look.

muted-editorial.notes: Magazine-photography restraint: saturation pulled to ~75%, faintly lifted blacks, cool shadows. Lets typography carry the colour.

teal-orange.notes: Cool shadows, warm highlights and skin; complementary separation of subject from background.

bleach-bypass.notes: A black-and-white layer overlaid on the colour image, as the retained silver does on film: muted colour, hard blacks, more grain.

film-fade.notes: Blacks never reach black, highlights roll off below white, warm cast. The 'Instagram film' look.

warm-film.notes: Soft contrast, warm midtones, slightly cyan-green shadows. Parametric: it suggests a portrait stock, it does not reproduce one. For a real stock, use a scanned .cube with --lut.

bright-pop.notes: Punchy colour and crisp detail for phone screens; pairs with heavy captions.

mono-classic.notes: Luminance-weighted greyscale with a firm S-curve. With one accent colour in the type it reads as Swiss poster photography.

noir.notes: Crushed shadows, bright accents, heavy vignette.

cross-process.notes: Shifted colours with yellow-green highlights and cyan-blue shadows, high contrast. Lomo / zine energy.

day-for-night.notes: Underexposed and pushed blue to read as moonlight.

cinestill-night.notes: Cool tungsten-balanced base with a red glow bleeding around the brightest highlights, as on film without an anti-halation layer. Made for night streets, neon and practical lights; on a bright daylight frame every highlight blooms, so pick it for low-key footage.

camcorder.notes: Bleeding chroma, soft detail, lifted blacks, noise. Reads as found footage; pair with a REC overlay and date stamp.
